title: Stripping, drying and reapplying emulsion polish on hard floors
audience: Trained cleaning operative assigned hard-floor finishing work, who will run a buffer and wet pick-up under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Describe the order of work for stripping old polish: outside edges first, small sections, slurry removed before it dries.
Inspect a buffer and wet pick-up for electrical and mechanical faults before and after use.
Choose a buffing pad by its colour and abrasiveness for the stage of the job.
Apply and cross-weave polish coats, letting each coat dry before the next, and explain how drying time affects slip risk.
Store the buffer and wet pick-up so the pad, base plate, blade and tank are not left in a state that damages the machine.

instruction.heading: Scope of the task
instruction.body: This lesson covers the full cycle for a hard floor finished with emulsion polish. The old polish film is loosened with a stripper and worked off with a rotary buffer. A wet pick-up machine then lifts the resulting slurry. The bare floor is dried and checked, and new polish is laid down in thin, even coats. The work happens in a single area, but its risks run through the whole job: chemical contact and fumes, an electrical lead near a spinning pad, a slip hazard on wet or freshly polished floor, and damage to the floor finish if the steps are done out of order. The operator must be trained on the machines before running them. This lesson does not authorise any plant use and does not replace the product's safety data sheet.

instruction.heading: Equipment checks before work starts
instruction.body: Check each electrical machine before switching it on. Confirm that the electrical safety test date is current and recorded on the site register. Look over the plug and the lead for cuts, cracks or bare conductors, and reject any lead that has been repaired with electrical tape. On the wet pick-up, check that the squeegee blade is intact and that the float is sound. Choose the buffing pad by colour. A darker pad is more abrasive than a lighter one, so pick the pad for the stage of the job as set in the approved method. Wash all equipment before any chemical is mixed or used, so that residue from an earlier product cannot react with the new one. Every chemical container must carry a legible manufacturer's label.

instruction.heading: Preparing the room
instruction.body: Cover any fittings, walls, skirting and surfaces that the stripper or polish could reach. Use plastic sheeting and secure it with masking tape. Open doors and windows where possible, because stripper vapour can be harmful and moving air helps the floor dry sooner. Put on gloves and eye protection before opening any container. Set up barriers so that no one walks across the floor while it is wet or unprotected.

instruction.heading: Stripping in sections
instruction.body: Work from the outside edges toward the centre. Apply stripper to the edges with an edging tool and let it sit for the contact time the manufacturer specifies. Wipe any stripper that has landed on the skirting boards so that chemical does not build up there. Next, mop stripper onto the central area, allow contact time, and scrub the film off with the buffer. Use overlapping figure-eight passes and move from the edges inward. Keep each section small enough that you can finish and clear it before the chemical dries. Pick up the slurry with the wet pick-up, working from dry floor toward wet floor, so you never step on liquid you have not yet cleared. Slurry must not be left to dry on the floor, because dried residue is much harder to remove and can leave marks.

instruction.heading: After stripping and before polishing
instruction.body: If a standard alkaline stripper was used, neutralise the floor as the procedure directs. The source method names vinegar for this; confirm the neutralising step against the product label before use. Once the polish film is gone, the floor is unprotected and will mark easily. Keep shoe soles clean and avoid walking back over treated areas. Let the floor dry completely and check that it is clean before any polish goes on. Rinse the wet pick-up's tank and wipe the blade before storing it.

instruction.heading: Applying the polish
instruction.body: Polish the outside edges of the room first, then let that band dry before working across the open floor. Apply polish with a mop using figure-eight overlapping sweeps across the middle. Keep polish off the outer edges during the main application. Wipe any polish that reaches the skirting boards straight away. Buff the floor between coats using the buffing method in the same procedure set. Wait until each coat is dry before applying the next. Lay the second coat at right angles to the first (cross-weave). Apply a third coat only if the surface still needs it. Remove the plastic sheeting only after the final coat is dry.

instruction.heading: Operating electrical machines safely
instruction.body: Keep the cord behind you so the spinning pad cannot run over it. Never drape the cord over your shoulder. A faulty machine could give an electric shock, and a snagged cord can pull you off balance. Keep the buffer under control at all times. Only trained operators run the machine. Electrical equipment must stay clean, maintained, tested and in good repair. Any machine that is damaged or whose test has lapsed comes out of service and is reported.

instruction.heading: Storage and end of use
instruction.body: Never store a buffer with the pad and base plate still fitted. Safety check the machine and damp wipe it after use. Store it upright with the base plate balanced on top. Wash the buffing pads and hang them to dry. Wash out the wet pick-up, wipe the blade, rinse the float and let everything dry. Wash buckets and cloths, store buckets upside down so they air-dry, and store all equipment in its colour group so clean and dirty items never mix.

procedure: Confirm the job scope and check the approved stripper, polish, neutraliser and pad for this floor.
Inspect the buffer and wet pick-up. Reject any damaged machine or lead and tag it out.
Wash the equipment before use and check that every chemical container has a readable label.
Cover fittings and surfaces that must not receive overspray, and tape the sheeting down.
Open ventilation where possible, put on gloves and eye protection, and set up barriers.
Apply stripper to the outside edges with an edging tool, allow contact time, and wipe any overspray from the skirting.
Apply stripper to the central area with a mop and allow contact time.
Scrub the film off with the buffer, working from the edges inward in overlapping figure-eight passes.
Pick up the slurry with the wet pick-up, dry to wet, in sections small enough to clear before drying.
Neutralise the floor if the product requires it, then let the floor dry completely.
Apply the first polish coat to the outside edges, let it dry, then apply it to the open floor.
Buff between coats, apply the second coat cross-woven, and let it dry. Apply a third coat only if needed.
Remove the plastic sheeting after the final coat is dry and wipe any skirting overspray.
Safety check the machines, wash and store the buffer upright with the pad removed, and wash out the wet pick-up.

workedExamples.situation: A corridor in a small office has three old polish coats and a visible scuff trail. The job is to strip, dry and reapply two coats of emulsion polish before the end of the day. The corridor is the only route between two offices.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you manage the route, the timing and the slurry?
workedExamples.reasoning: Barrier off only the working section and keep a clear route open at the other end. Work in short sections so each one is cleared while still wet. Allow each polish coat to dry before the next. If the programme cannot allow proper drying before the deadline, tell the supervisor and agree a revised timing. Do not squeeze in coats that are still wet.

workedExamples.situation: After stripping one section, a worker notices a torn blade on the wet pick-up and a taped repair near the plug of the buffer.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which equipment can be used, and what happens next?
workedExamples.reasoning: A torn blade leaves liquid on the floor and makes pick-up unreliable, so the wet pick-up must not be used until the blade is replaced. The taped lead is unsafe. Tag the buffer out of service, report both faults, and do not keep working with the buffer until it has been checked.

equipmentAndPpe: Rotary buffer with colour-coded buffing pads
Wet pick-up machine with blade and float
Edging tool and mop for stripper and polish
Stripper, polish and neutraliser as approved for the floor
Gloves suited to the product, and eye protection
Ventilation: doors and windows opened where possible

commonErrors.error: Leaving slurry to dry on the floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Pick up slurry while it is wet, and work in sections small enough to clear in one pass.

commonErrors.error: Applying polish to the open floor before the edges have dried.
commonErrors.prevention: Polish the outside edges first, let them dry, then move to the open floor.

commonErrors.error: Storing the buffer with the pad or base plate still fitted.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the pad and base plate, check and wash them, then store the machine upright.

commonErrors.error: Walking on a stripped or freshly polished floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Barrier the area and keep shoe soles clean until the floor is dry.

commonErrors.error: Running the cord under the pad or across the working path.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the cord behind you at all times and check it before each pass.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Only trained operators run the buffer and wet pick-up. Operator training is required before use. Completing this lesson does not certify you to operate the equipment.
Stripper, polish and neutraliser are hazardous chemicals. Follow the label and safety data sheet for dilution, contact time, PPE and ventilation.
Electrical equipment must be tested and tagged, or inspected, under the local rule. The source names PAT testing.
Stop work and tag out the machine if the lead is damaged, the test status is unknown or lapsed, or the pad or blade is faulty.

qualityStandard: Edges and skirting are free of stripper and polish overspray after each stage.
No slurry, residue or old polish film remains in the work area once the floor is dry.
The dried floor shows an even finish with no streaks, ridges or sticky patches.
Each polish coat is dry before the next is applied, and the second coat is cross-woven.
All equipment is washed, the pad is removed from the buffer, and the machine is stored upright.
documentationEvidence: Equipment check record, including the electrical test status and any machine tagged out
Product names and label references for stripper, neutraliser and polish used
Number of polish coats applied and drying time between coats
Before and after photographs of the floor in good light
Any fault, spill or near miss recorded on the job sheet
summary: Strip from the outside edges inward, in small sections, and pick up the slurry before it dries.
Check the buffer and wet pick-up before use, and tag out any damaged lead or blade.
Polish the edges first, buff between coats, and cross-weave the second coat once each coat is dry.
Store the buffer upright with the pad and base plate removed, and wash out the wet pick-up after use.

knowledgeChecks.question: When stripping old polish from a hard floor, which area should be worked first?
options: The middle of the room, so the slurry can be moved out to the edges
The outside edges of the area, so the edging is handled before the open floor
The doorway, so the operator can leave quickly at the end of the job
Whichever corner is nearest the wet pick-up bucket

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must slurry, the mix of removed polish and stripper, not be left to dry on the floor?
options: It makes the buffing pad lose its colour
Once dry it is much harder to remove and can leave marks on the bare floor
Slurry dries softer, so drying it on the floor makes it easier to remove
It stops new polish from bonding even after the floor is dry

knowledgeChecks.question: A buffer's lead has a taped repair near the plug and its electrical test date has passed. What should the operator do?
options: Use the buffer for a small area only, since the job is short
Re-tape the lead and note the repair on the job sheet
Tag the machine out of service and report it for testing or repair
Fit a residual-current device to the lead and continue the job
